reply_text:
I found one weak candidate for 2019 and no firm, dated AI prediction. In a CNBC report of the New York Times New Work Summit on February 25, 2019, Altman said the world must be "ready for" global GDP growing 50 percent a year "for a couple of decades." That gives a span of time, but he framed it as something to prepare for rather than a forecast, and it is about the economy that AI would produce. I saw it only in that news report, and a checker may well reject it. I didn't come across the claim already on file (2019-01-05, AGI by 2025), so I couldn't confirm or add to it.

- **Radiologist line (Feb 2019):** this is the one people usually cite, but it describes the present ("are already much worse") and names no date.
- **StrictlyVC interview (May 2019):** TechCrunch's write-up quotes him on AGI ("ask it to figure out a way to make an investment return," "capture the light cone of all future value"), but none of it gives a date. I didn't watch the video of the full interview. The Podcast Notes summary page returned only site menus and none of the notes.
- **Microsoft deal (Jul 2019):** the New York Times story, reprinted in the Irish Times, quotes him on AGI without any timeline. It reports in its own words that Altman "admits OpenAI may never get there."
- **OpenAI LP Hacker News thread (Mar 2019):** the page I opened had the usernames stripped, so I couldn't tell which comments were his.

A note on how the searches ran: my code crashed after the first fixed search, but that search had already finished and I didn't run it again. All three fixed searches ran once each, and I used all 12 searches and all 6 page openings.
